added.title: Founding AI Robotics Engineer
added.description:
Base Comp:
 $220k - $520k

Total Comp:
 $360k up to $3.4M+ for exceptional performance (with major milestone bonuses up to $3.4M+ for achieving SOTA contact-rich manipulation and other SOTA robotics targets)

The Opportunity

Newtson Industries is hiring a Founding AI Robotics Engineer to work alongside Inventor & CEO Dylan Gastel, our Founding AI Researcher, and our Founding Robotics Hardware and Mechatronics Engineers to build and train the intelligence brain behind Newtson's robotics team. Our ambition is to build the best robot in the world, and our overarching technical goal is to achieve SOTA contact-rich dexterous manipulation across real-world physical tasks. As our first short-term proving target on the path to SOTA manipulation, we are sprinting to catch a high-speed football pass from an NFL quarterback better than any wide receiver and better than any other robot in the world before the Super Bowl. Newtson is in the business of inventing technologies that are #1 in the world. You will play a defining role in making history.

How We Operate

Newtson is building a team of S-tier individual contributors who operate as CEOs of their own internal startup, advancing their key initiative within the greater business. We are not seeking senior-level executives who wish to build a large org to manage. We are seeking the hungriest, highest-output individuals who believe their potential is at least 10 times higher than their current compensation structure allows for. If you are the type of person who feels like you can do the work of 10 of your peers, and you wish to be compensated accordingly, Newtson is the place for you. If you feel like you have something to prove, we don't care what it is — we will help you prove it.

Qualifications

Newtson Industries is seeking an individual with the following qualifications:

You are fired up to own building and training the brain behind the best robot in the world — with SOTA contact-rich manipulation as the main mission and our Super Bowl pass-catching milestone as the immediate proving ground.
You understand that your primary contribution is training and deploying real-time perception, prediction, and control policies that push physical robots past current SOTA manipulation limits.
You are a powerful sole contributor eager to collaborate, yet you understand that our success often hinges on your ability to put your head down and just Do Your Job.
You buckle in to grind when needed, and you appreciate that Newtson rewards high output over hard work.
You value the importance of working together, in person, and you will be a strong contributor to team camaraderie, collaboration, and creativity.
You are eager to join a company run like a professional sports team — contribute significantly and you will be significantly rewarded. Mediocrity does not win championships and will be replaced. You are here to win championships.
You bring proven industry experience OR raw, S-tier talent and execution speed across the required job functions — we pay for output, not years on a resume.
You will thrive at a company of Newtson's size — with approximately ten total employees and where you may be the only individual in your department.
You are fearless, yet you take a practical, data-driven approach to risk taking.
You are creative, yet you are comfortable executing repetitive or mundane tasks.
You dream big and frequently voice your ideas, yet you have the humility to know that your ideas will not always prevail.
You usually find the correct answer yourself, yet you have the self-awareness to know when to ask for help.
You are honest, genuine, and care about your individual success and performance, yet you will be selfless and will put the success of the greater entity before that of yourself, knowing that your teammates are doing the same.
You are confident that if chosen for this role, this will be your best career decision.
Your friends, family, and colleagues would overwhelmingly agree with the above statements.

About the Role

You own building, training, and deploying the brain behind Newtson's robots. Your primary goal is achieving SOTA contact-rich manipulation — mastering high-speed, force-sensitive physical interaction on real hardware and scaling those capabilities across American factory floors, with $3.4M+ upside directly tied to hitting SOTA contact-rich manipulation and subsequent SOTA robotics benchmarks. Catching 60 mph NFL passes before the Super Bowl is our short-term target designed to force ultra-low-latency perception, tactile feedback, and dynamic control under real impact loads. You take learning-based and optimal-control policies from simulation and proprietary factory datasets and run them deterministically on hardware under strict 50 to 200 ms budgets.

Required Skills

Robot Brain & SOTA Control

Train and deploy imitation learning, reinforcement learning, VLA, and optimal-control policies directly onto fast, contact-rich multi-axis robots.
Build ultra-low-latency 3D perception, tracking, state estimation, and trajectory prediction pipelines in C++ and Python.
Fuse high-frequency tactile arrays (2,500 Hz), joint encoders, and high-speed vision to solve contact-rich grasping, in-hand manipulation, and dynamic impacts.
Optimize on-robot model inference using CUDA, TensorRT, and C++ to hold hard real-time control loop budgets without jitter.

Work Style

Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the CEO, Founding AI Researcher, Robotics Hardware and Mechatronics Engineers, and Test Quarterback beside the physical robot until reliability approaches 100%.
Own the full loop from simulation and policy training to real-robot deployment without throwing models over a wall.
Combine S-tier research taste for SOTA breakthroughs with pragmatic engineering speed for immediate hardware milestones.

Preferred

Shipped SOTA or near-SOTA real-world policies on dexterous hands, contact-rich manipulators, humanoids, or high-speed dynamic robots.
Deep proficiency in MuJoCo, Isaac Lab, PyTorch, high-speed multi-camera geometry, tactile learning, and real-time Linux.

How to Apply

Send your resume, Google Scholar or GitHub, and 2 to 3 videos of policies or control stacks you personally trained and deployed on real physical robot hardware — along with what broke during sim-to-real transfer and how you solved it.

Email your application to careers@newtson.com.

Newtson Industries is headquartered in San Francisco at the heart of Union St in Cow Hollow. This is an in-person role.

added.title: Google Agentic AI Delivery Specialist
added.description:
We are:

A leading partner to the world’s major cloud providers, including AWS, Azure, and Google. The formation of Accenture Cloud First, with a $3 billion investment over three years, demonstrates our commitment to deliver greater value to our clients when they need it most and offers huge growth opportunities for you! Our Cloud First group of more than 70,000 cloud professionals delivers a full stack of integrated cloud capabilities across data, edge, integrated infrastructure and applications, deep ecosystem skills, culture of change along with a deep industry expertise to shape, move, build and operate our clients’ businesses in the cloud. To accelerate our customers transformation leveraging cloud, we combine world-class learning and talent development expertise; deep experience in cloud change management; and cloud-ready operating models with a commitment to responsible business by design — with security, data privacy, responsible use of artificial intelligence, sustainability and ethics and compliance built into the fundamental changes Accenture helps companies achieve.

About the Role: Building the Future in the Age of Agents

Join the elite technical and product engine of the Accenture Google Business Group (AGBG). We are not a traditional project delivery organization; we are a practice of innovators and builders guiding our clients through the most significant shift in technology: the move to Agentic AI and Product-Led Operating Models. As a Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Agentic AI Delivery Engineer, you are a new breed of technologist—a "product-minded engineer" who is as fluent in the language of code as you are in the language of customer outcomes. You don't just build solutions; you leverage the best of technologies Google Cloud has to offer for client requirements, helping clients break free from legacy solution mindset and practices to build truly modern, value-driven software products on Google Cloud.

You Are:

A passionate, hands-on GCP specialist/practitioner who understands that great software is not just about elegant code, but about solving real problems leveraging the best technology tools available for a client. You are as comfortable building a multi-agent workflow on Vertex AI as you are testing a solution built by other team members in a compressed timeline, leveraging the various tools and technologies of Google Cloud. You have a consultative mindset and a deep curiosity to understand the "why" behind a client's business requirements and convert them to an optimal technology solution. You are an evangelist for modern ways of working, grounded in the principles of Product-Led engineering and operating models and related approaches. You are an exceptional communicator, great team player, continuous learner and a true believer in continual change.

The Work:

As a GCP Agentic AI Delivery Engineer, you will be a technical and product-centric engineer in consulting and engineering projects, customizing Google Cloud Agentic solutions for client requirements. You will partner with Accenture's global delivery teams by providing superior technical expertise and product innovation skills. Your role is to execute complex technology solutions for our clients by designing, building, and demonstrating Agentic AI solutions. You will act as a trusted team player, guiding others in the team on how to adopt a Product Engineering mindset and be the expert on specific Google Cloud technologies/products.

Key Responsibilities:

Outcome-Driven Design and Build: Actively participate in technical discovery workshops to translate client business requirements into GCP technology design elements and customized solutions. Design, build, test and deploy innovative, agentic-first solutions on GCP that are directly tied to the client business requirements.

Hands-On Development & Proof-of-Value: Rapidly design, build, and present compelling proof-of-concept (POC) solutions that bring your Google Cloud proficiency to workable solutions. This includes hands-on software engineering using Vertex AI, Gemini/Agentic AI, BigQuery, Google Data technologies, Terraform, and modern CI/CD practices.

Product-Led Project delivery: Act as an agile SME/coach on modern software development. Guide and enable the delivery team on the principles of the Product Agile Operating Model and how to structure delivery sprints for continuous delivery using Google Cloud Technologies.

Team Collaboration: Ability to travel as needed for project meetings, workshops, client discussions, etc., Working with global teams and leveraging the various collaborative tools and channels for project delivery and status reporting.

Travel may be required for this role. The amount of travel will vary from 0 to 100% depending on business need and client requirements.

Here's What You Need

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate’s Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience).

Minimum of 3 years of experience in a hands-on, client-facing technology role (e.g., Google Cloud Engineer, Product Engineer, Technology Consultant).

Minimum of 3 years of deep, hands-on experience architecting and building solutions on GCP.

Minimum of 2 years of experience interacting with project team members distributed across the globe. Well versed in project management methodologies and product/project testing methodologies.

Minimum of 2 years of proven experience on Google Cloud technologies OR Minimum of 1 years of implementation experience on EITHER Agentic systems, leveraging Google Gemini Enterprise, Microsoft Azure Foundry, Microsoft Co-Pilot and/or AWS Bedrock OR on Agentic systems and Google Gemini Enterprise Partner Specialist certifications (CPS)

Bonus points if you have

Product & Agile Mindset: Hands-on experience working within a Product Operating Model. Practical experience in delivering agile projects, contributing to sprint-based deliverables and outcomes.

Consulting & Innovation Acumen: Experience participating in client-facing innovation workshops and converting ideas into outcome-focused solutions. World-class communication skills to articulate project status and delivery challenges and issues to project leadership and client audiences.

Agentic AI & Software Product Engineering: Proven experience architecting and building agentic workflows using Vertex AI. Deep understanding of agentic components, including reasoning engines, planning, tool use, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Hands-on expertise with Google's Gemini models. A commitment to software engineering best practices, including CI/CD, automated testing, and building secure, scalable products.

Technical Depth: Google Cloud Professional certifications (e.g., Professional Cloud Architect, Professional Machine Learning Engineer, Professional Data Engineer, GenAI Leader). Project experience across the GCP ecosystem, including GKE, BigQuery, Vertex AI, CES, Apigee, and other GCP technologies.

added.description:
About Accenture:

Accenture helps the world's leading enterprises reinvent by building their digital core and unleashing the power of AI to create value at speed for organizations across industries. Our strategy is to be the reinvention partner of choice for our clients and lead in the safe, widespread adoption of AI, and to be the most client-focused, AI-enabled, great place to work in the world. We bring together the talent of our approximately 814,000 people with proprietary assets and platforms, deep process and industry expertise, and leading ecosystem relationships to deliver end-to-end solutions and measurable outcomes at scale. Through our Reinvention Services, we offer broad expertise across Cybersecurity, Digital Core, Finance, Industry and Enterprise, Song, Supply Chain and Engineering, and Talent, with advanced capabilities in AI and Data, Industry and Process, and Technology. We serve approximately 9,000 clients and generated approximately $74 billion in FY26 revenue. Visit us at accenture.com.

We Are:

Accenture LearnVantage helps organizations transform how their people learn and work. We partner with enterprise clients to design and deliver high-quality, scalable, outcome-driven learning that builds the skills their workforces need. Udacity, now part of Accenture LearnVantage, brings deep expertise in technical upskilling through hands-on, project-based online learning. Together we build learning experiences that help people gain in-demand skills in data science, machine learning, AI, and more.

You Are:

You are a technical learning content developer who turns data science expertise into learning experiences that stick. You combine hands-on work in Python, statistics, and machine learning with a grounding in how adults learn, and you judge your own content by whether learners can demonstrably apply the skill in a real-world setting. You own the technical accuracy and instructional quality of what you build, you use AI tooling to work faster without dropping the quality bar, and you collaborate well with subject matter experts, authors, and testers. You are the first person through your own material, so you find the gaps a learner would hit before a learner does. You move toward solutions even when requirements are ambiguous, guided by data but biased toward action.

The Work:

Join the Learning Experience team and help build the data science learning experiences that power effective workforce upskilling at enterprise scale. As a Technical Content Developer, Data Science, you’ll take design requirements and learning objectives from the curriculum roadmap and partner with subject matter experts to build course modules, hands-on labs, projects, and assessments. You’ll own the technical accuracy and instructional quality of what you produce so that learners can demonstrably apply new data science skills on the job.

Develop technical learning experiences (courses, modules, hands-on labs, projects, quizzes, and assessments) against defined design requirements and learning objectives for the data science domain.

Author and test hands-on labs, notebooks, and projects end to end, making sure datasets and coding environments are configured correctly and working solutions are reproducible by every learner.

Build assessments, quizzes, and other instructional-design elements that measure whether the target skill was actually acquired, in line with LearnVantage learning standards.

Validate the technical accuracy of all content, partnering with subject matter experts and authors to keep pace with changes in data science libraries, platforms, and industry practice.

Coach new authors through the course development process and give pedagogical feedback on their content from the learner’s perspective.

Use AI tooling to accelerate drafting, iteration, and QA of content, raising throughput without sacrificing quality.

Incorporate feedback from testers, learners, and reviewers into content revisions, and use learner outcome data to improve course effectiveness.

In this role, you’ll work in a curriculum pod and report into a Technical Curriculum Lead. This position is US remote.

What’s In It for You?

You’ll build data science learning that reaches people at enterprise scale and gives them skills they can apply on the job.

You’ll work at the leading edge of AI-accelerated content development, helping shape the tooling and workflows the pipeline depends on.

Accenture will continually invest in your craft and growth, with access to certifications, learning resources, and a global community of practitioners.

You’ll collaborate with subject matter experts, authors, and testers across the Accenture LearnVantage team.

Travel may be required for role. 0-80% depending on client and business needs.

Here’s What You Need:

Minimum 3 years of professional experience in data science or data analytics, including data wrangling, exploratory data analysis, data visualization, statistical modeling, and machine learning, using Python (including NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn) and SQL.

Minimum 3 years of experience in instructional design, curriculum development, or teaching technical content to adult learners, grounded in adult learning science (scaffolding, retrieval practice, cognitive load, and assessment).

Minimum 3 years of experience with AI tooling for drafting, iteration, and QA.

Minimum 1 year of experience with version control tools like Git.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate's Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience).

Bonus Points If:

You have experience authoring and testing hands-on labs or projects end to end, including container (Docker) and VM environment troubleshooting.

You have experience building dashboards or reporting in Tableau, Power BI, or advanced spreadsheets.

You have experience with cloud-based tools for data workflows such as AWS SageMaker, Azure Data Factory, Snowflake, or Databricks.

You have experience with big data tools such as Apache Spark or distributed databases.

You have experience designing and analyzing A/B tests.

You have experience developing asynchronous online course content.

You combine hands-on work in Python, statistics, and machine learning with a grounding in how adults learn, and you judge your own content by whether learners can demonstrably apply the skill in a real-world setting. You own the technical accuracy and instructional quality of what you build, you use AI tooling to work faster without dropping the quality bar, and you collaborate well with subject matter experts, authors, and testers. You are the first person through your own material, so you find the gaps a learner would hit before a learner does. You move toward solutions even when requirements are ambiguous, guided by data but biased toward action.

The Work:

Join the Learning Experience team and help build the data science learning experiences that power effective workforce upskilling at enterprise scale. As a Technical Content Developer, Data Science, you’ll take design requirements and learning objectives from the curriculum roadmap and partner with subject matter experts to build course modules, hands-on labs, projects, and assessments. You’ll own the technical accuracy and instructional quality of what you produce so that learners can demonstrably apply new data science skills on the job.

Develop technical learning experiences (courses, modules, hands-on labs, projects, quizzes, and assessments) against defined design requirements and learning objectives for the data science domain.

Author and test hands-on labs, notebooks, and projects end to end, making sure datasets and coding environments are configured correctly and working solutions are reproducible by every learner.

Build assessments, quizzes, and other instructional-design elements that measure whether the target skill was actually acquired, in line with LearnVantage learning standards.

Validate the technical accuracy of all content, partnering with subject matter experts and authors to keep pace with changes in data science libraries, platforms, and industry practice.

Coach new authors through the course development process and give pedagogical feedback on their content from the learner’s perspective.

Use AI tooling to accelerate drafting, iteration, and QA of content, raising throughput without sacrificing quality.

Incorporate feedback from testers, learners, and reviewers into content revisions, and use learner outcome data to improve course effectiveness.

In this role, you’ll work in a curriculum pod and report into a Technical Curriculum Lead. This position is US remote.

What’s In It for You?

You’ll build data science learning that reaches people at enterprise scale and gives them skills they can apply on the job.

You’ll work at the leading edge of AI-accelerated content development, helping shape the tooling and workflows the pipeline depends on.

Accenture will continually invest in your craft and growth, with access to certifications, learning resources, and a global community of practitioners.

You’ll collaborate with subject matter experts, authors, and testers across the Accenture LearnVantage team.

Travel may be required for role. 0-80% depending on client and business needs.

Here’s What You Need:

Minimum 3 years of professional experience in data science or data analytics, including data wrangling, exploratory data analysis, data visualization, statistical modeling, and machine learning, using Python (including NumPy, pandas, and scikit-learn) and SQL.

Minimum 3 years of experience in instructional design, curriculum development, or teaching technical content to adult learners, grounded in adult learning science (scaffolding, retrieval practice, cognitive load, and assessment).

Minimum 3 years of experience with AI tooling for drafting, iteration, and QA.

Minimum 1 year of experience with version control tools like Git.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent (minimum 12 years) work experience. (If Associate's Degree, must have minimum 6 years work experience).

Bonus Points If:

You have experience authoring and testing hands-on labs or projects end to end, including container (Docker) and VM environment troubleshooting.

You have experience building dashboards or reporting in Tableau, Power BI, or advanced spreadsheets.

You have experience with cloud-based tools for data workflows such as AWS SageMaker, Azure Data Factory, Snowflake, or Databricks.

You have experience with big data tools such as Apache Spark or distributed databases.

You have experience designing and analyzing A/B tests.

You have experience developing asynchronous online course content.

added.title: Applied AI Architect - EDU
added.description:
About The Team

The AI Architect team partners with organizations to turn OpenAI's most capable models into meaningful, real-world impact. We work with customers across industries and digital-native businesses to identify where AI can create value, design secure and scalable solutions, and help those solutions move from early exploration into sustained production adoption. The team brings together technical strategy, customer partnership, and practical deployment expertise, working closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Research, and specialist delivery teams.

Within Education, we partner with universities, schools, research institutions, and countrywide education systems to advance responsible, mission-aligned uses of AI. These environments require more than technical deployment: success depends on institutional trust, thoughtful governance, stakeholder education, change management, and a value narrative that resonates with academic leaders, researchers, IT teams, faculty, administrators, and students.

About The Role

As an Applied AI Architect for Education, you will be the senior technical owner for a named portfolio of education customers and the primary technical counterpart to their leadership teams. You will act as the “CTO of your book of business,” shaping each institution’s AI strategy and guiding its journey from pre-sales discovery and solution evaluation through deployment, adoption, and measurable institutional impact.

You will own the technical account plan across ChatGPT Edu, the OpenAI API, Codex, and other agentic AI solutions. In partnership with the Account Director, you will translate institutional priorities into a focused portfolio of use cases, an actionable adoption roadmap, and a clear path to durable value and growth. The Account Director owns the commercial strategy; you own the technical strategy, customer journey, and path to production value.

You will work across academic, research, administrative, and operational contexts—helping customers determine where AI can responsibly improve teaching and learning, accelerate research, strengthen student and faculty services, and make institutional operations more effective. You will account for the realities of education environments, including shared governance, complex stakeholder networks, academic calendars, accessibility, data privacy, responsible-AI expectations, and the need to build confidence among communities with differing levels of AI readiness.

You will remain accountable for the technical outcome while bringing in the right specialists across deployment, implementation, enablement, security, product, education programs, and partners. This role calls for strong education-sector fluency, sound architectural judgment, and the ability to move confidently between executive strategy, academic and operational workflows, and hands-on technical conversations.

In This Role, You Will

Serve as the primary technical advisor and long-term technical relationship owner for a named portfolio of existing education customers and pre-sales prospects.
Partner with Account Directors on account strategy while owning the technical account plan, technical milestones, adoption priorities, value-realization path, and expansion opportunities.
Lead discovery with institutional executives, academic leaders, researchers, faculty, administrators, and technical teams to identify and prioritize use cases connected to meaningful institutional objectives.
Translate education priorities into clear Applied AI Architectures spanning models, applications, institutional data, identity, integrations, security, privacy, governance, evaluation, and deployment.
Guide institutions through technical evaluations, demonstrations, workshops, prototypes, and proofs of value, building confidence in both the solution and its responsible path to production.
Translate institutional objectives into actionable adoption roadmaps with clear workstreams, sequencing, milestones, stakeholder ownership, governance, risks, success measures, and change-management needs.
Develop a focused use-case portfolio across areas such as teaching and learning, research, student and faculty services, knowledge management, software development, and administrative operations.
Translate institutional objectives into actionable adoption roadmaps with clear workstreams, sequencing, milestones, stakeholder ownership, governance, risks, success measures, and change-management needs.
Build trusted relationships and technical champions across CIOs, CTOs, CISOs, provosts, deans, research leaders, faculty, administrators, and other institutional stakeholders.
Qualify and coordinate support from Deployment Engineering, implementation, training and enablement, Product, Research, education specialists, partners, and other delivery teams.
Remain accountable for technical progress and customer outcomes while ensuring delivery teams own implementation execution once engaged.
Track adoption, usage, account health, production readiness, and measurable customer impact, intervening early when risks threaten value realization.
Identify repeatable education patterns and reusable architectures that can accelerate responsible adoption across institutions, departments, campuses, and education systems.
Translate field insights into actionable feedback for Product, Engineering, and Research, representing the needs and production patterns of education customers.
Help identify expansion opportunities where OpenAI can support additional academic, research, administrative, or operational workflows.

You Might Thrive In This Role If You

Have significant experience in customer-facing technical roles such as solutions architecture, solutions engineering, technical account leadership, AI deployment, or technical customer success.
Have guided complex organizations from technical evaluation through production adoption and measurable value realization.
Build credibility with senior technical and business leaders while communicating equally well with hands-on engineers.
Bring strong software and cloud architecture foundations, including APIs, distributed systems, data integration, identity, security, and privacy.
Understand modern AI systems, frontier LLM models, agentic applications, model evaluation, retrieval, or enterprise AI workflows.
Can prototype, explain technical tradeoffs, and work confidently with APIs, SDKs, and languages such as Python or JavaScript.
Exercise sound judgment about when to go deep personally, when to involve specialists, and how to define clear handoffs and ownership.
Have experience developing technical account plans, prioritizing complex customer portfolios, and connecting adoption to measurable outcomes.
Can translate technical capabilities into institutional value across priorities such as student success, research productivity, faculty enablement, administrative effectiveness, accessibility, risk, and governance.
Communicate clearly and can turn ambiguity, competing stakeholder needs, and complex technical choices into a practical narrative, executive decision, or action plan.
Work collaboratively across disciplines and care deeply about helping education institutions deploy advanced AI safely, responsibly, and in service of their missions.
Meaningful experience with education technology, higher education, K–12 systems, research institutions, or similarly mission-driven and consensus-oriented environments is an added bonus

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement.

Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations.

added.title: Forward Deployed Growth Partner, NAM
added.description:
About Hilbert

Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes. From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z).

Forward Deployed Growth Engineers are a new, dedicated customer team at Hilbert, sitting in our Foundations Tribe. You'll work hand in hand with our Growth Science and Product teams, who own the product's logic, models and playbooks, and take that expertise into every customer, from the first meeting to the moment Hilbert is running their growth.

What the role is

This is customer success delivered with growth expertise. You'll join each of your accounts as soon as the lead comes in. You'll help shape the use cases during the sales cycle and keep owning the account through deployment and live usage. You own two commercial outcomes: proof-of-concept conversion

and existing account revenue growth

. We also measure time to first value, sustained product adoption and the share of routine customer needs you handle independently.

Two things make this role different from most customer success jobs. First, you're forward-deployed: you'll travel with our GTM team around 50% of the time, sit in the room with our customers' leadership, and become the person they call when they want to move faster. Second, you're a growth operator, not a ticket handler: our customers buy growth, and you'll help them own their use cases in Hilbert, from paid media, CRM and retention to discounts, merchandising and demand forecasting, and read the results back with them . You are expected to develop a deep understanding of Hilbert’s capabilities, communicate clearly and effectively with customers, and proactively manage customer relationships to maximize the value delivered to every customer.

You'll be part of the first cohort of this team, reporting to the Head of Forward Deployed Growth in our Foundations Tribe and working day to day with the GTM team and delivery engineering pod in your region. You'll learn our data sources, deployment methods and the problems our customers bring us alongside our Growth Science, Product and data teams, and you'll handle most routine customer needs independently. When an account needs deeper expertise, you'll bring in our subject-matter experts and turn what you learn into answers, case studies and examples the whole team reuses.

What you'll do

Own a portfolio of accounts end-to-end: get assigned as soon as a lead comes in, shape the use cases with GTM and sales engineering through close, and stay accountable for onboarding coordination, customer follow-ups and blocker tracking.
Convert pilots into long-term partnerships: define success criteria with the customer up front, keep the proof of concept on track, and make the business case for expansion with numbers you can defend.
Grow account revenue: find the next highest-impact use case inside each customer and turn it into new scope.
Be the customer's trusted growth advisor: lead demos and working sessions, help customers put agreed use cases into practice, train their teams, review results, and identify what is blocking adoption.
Drive real business transformation: go beyond usage and make sure the results change how the customer's business runs.
Get the customer's data in: scope the data each use case needs, agree with their data team how it reaches Hilbert, and run the timeline with our data engineers until it is usable. Do it again whenever a new use case needs new data.
Capture how each customer measures their business: their KPIs, definitions and business rules, set up in Hilbert so every answer matches their numbers.
Manage every stakeholder: from the C-level sponsor to the marketing, growth and data teams who use Hilbert every day, and keep them aligned as the account grows.
Build rapport in person: travel with our GTM team around 50% of the time, shadow and then lead customer sessions, and know the product better than anyone else in the room.
Cover most customer needs yourself, and know when to escalate: you are expected to handle around 80% of customer needs independently from the very first assignment, building toward the capability to cover 95% of everything a customer brings. For everything else, engage our Growth Science, Product, and Data teams efficiently by providing clear customer context, business impact, relevant evidence, and what you have already investigated. Respect their time by minimizing unnecessary meetings and prioritizing clear, asynchronous communication. Own the follow-up, keep the customer informed, and ensure key learnings feed into the product roadmap.
Expand across departments and use cases: map which other teams (paid media, CRM, merchandising, pricing, finance) can run their decisions on Hilbert, find the next highest-impact use case in each, and turn it into new scope.
Embed Hilbert into activation surfaces: connect Hilbert’s outputs to the tools where the customer’s teams already act, from ad platforms and CRM/CDP to promo, merchandising and planning systems, so every insight flows straight into execution and becomes part of the daily workflow.
Join GTM funnel reviews: take part in the regular funnel reviews with the GTM team, and know which leads are coming to you next.
Grow the shared library: add answers, case studies and customer examples, so expert guidance becomes something the whole team reuses.

What you bring

Around 5 to 8 years of experience: an engineering or natural sciences background, followed by an analytical role in management consulting or a similar setting; pure customer success leaders with a strong analytical edge are also welcome.
Strongly analytical: you write SQL and understand customer data sources, key business definitions, data coverage and freshness, and the meaning and limitations of model outputs well enough to explain them and investigate routine questions. You can build a business case and present it to a CFO or CMO.
Driven by real business transformation: insight isn't enough until it changes how the customer's business runs.
Continuous learning: you don't know insurance or grocery yet, and you'll figure it out fast. You're a problem solver who hacks most of the job yourself and knows exactly who to bring in for the rest.
Excellent with customers: polished and high-energy, at ease in every customer conversation from small talk to the boardroom, credible with senior stakeholders, and able to build relationships that outlast a single project.
Strong stakeholder management is a must: you navigate complex organizations and keep senior and day-to-day stakeholders aligned.
Happy to travel often across your region, around 50% of the time and sometimes to a different customer city every week, and to work with an owner's mindset in a fast-moving startup.
Nice to have: deep vertical expertise in retail, grocery, or financial services, or existing relationships with enterprise B2C companies.

Reporting and location

You report to the Head of Forward Deployed Growth and work closely with the Head of GTM, North America, as the growth counterpart to the region’s GTM team. You’re on the move with GTM, joining new leads and customer meetings from the first conversation. Our Growth Science and Product teams own the product’s logic, models and playbooks, train you on them and support you on the deepest problems, and the delivery engineering pod in North America builds and runs each deployment with you. You are based in our New York or San Francisco office, hybrid, with travel to customers across the region of around 50 percent.

Compensation

Base salary, plus variable pay tied to performance and the revenue you help drive (proof-of-concept conversion, renewals and expansion), plus equity. Details are shared in next steps.

Interview process

Recruiter screen, 30 minutes.
GTM interview with the Head of GTM, North America, 30 minutes: a customer relationship you owned, from first meeting to live usage or expansion, and how you managed the stakeholders along the way.
Hiring manager interview, 30 minutes: how you work with customers and with our Growth, Product and GTM teams.
Growth case with our Growth team, 60 minutes: a real customer case, from the business problem and the data it needs to the use case, the success criteria and the business case for expansion.
Team and final interviews: meet the people you’ll work with day to day, and our leadership.

VetsEZ is seeking a Senior AI Application Engineer to design, develop, and implement enterprise Artificial Intelligence (AI) solutions supporting the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The initial assignment will support the Joint Longitudinal Viewer (JLV) AI Summarization initiative, delivering a secure, governed AI-assisted search and summarization capability within an approved test environment utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Large Language Models (LLMs), and Amazon Bedrock, while supporting clinical evaluation and future production readiness.

Working closely with AI Solution Architects, Product Owners, cybersecurity teams, DevSecOps engineers, and clinical stakeholders, this individual will develop secure, scalable, and maintainable AI-powered applications that integrate seamlessly with existing enterprise healthcare systems while ensuring compliance with Federal security, privacy, and AI governance requirements.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and implement enterprise AI applications utilizing Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Develop AI-assisted search, summarization, and question-answering capabilities using Amazon Bedrock.
Build reusable AI services supporting prompt orchestration, document retrieval, and response generation.
Implement prompt engineering and source-grounding strategies to improve AI accuracy, consistency, traceability, and clinical relevance, including source links that support human verification.
Optimize AI performance while balancing response quality, latency, and operational cost.
Design and develop secure, scalable cloud-native applications utilizing modern software engineering practices.
Develop RESTful APIs and backend services supporting AI capabilities and enterprise integrations.
Implement approved document retrieval, vector search, and semantic search capabilities within the selected patient context and CHSD document set.

Implement logging, monitoring, audit capabilities, and operational telemetry, including model and prompt version tracking, usage and cost monitoring, and controls to detect model, prompt, retrieval, and data drift.

Collaborate with architects, product owners, clinicians, cybersecurity teams, and Government stakeholders throughout the software development lifecycle.

added.title: Senior Scientist, Machine Learning and Algorithm Development for RNA Design
added.description:
The Role

Moderna is seeking a computational scientist to develop artificial intelligence, machine-learning, deep-learning, and optimization methods for therapeutic mRNA design.

This is a hands-on research role centered on translating biological questions into computational problems, developing and rigorously evaluating new algorithms, and turning those methods into reusable scientific software. The successful candidate will develop predictive and generative models that connect mRNA sequence and structure with experimentally measured properties.

The ideal candidate combines depth in AI/ML and algorithm development with the ability to reason about biological sequence and structure. Direct RNA or mRNA experience is highly valued, but we also welcome strong computational method developers from adjacent areas of biology who can demonstrate how their expertise transfers to RNA design.

Here’s What You’ll Do

Formulate mRNA design challenges as well-defined machine-learning and optimization problems, including appropriate objectives, constraints, datasets, and evaluation strategies.
Develop and benchmark predictive, generative, and optimization methods for biological sequence and structure.
Integrate mRNA sequence, predicted or experimentally measured structure, and high-throughput assay data into computational models.
Work closely with RNA biologists and experimental teams to design informative experiments, interpret results, and iteratively improve models.
Evaluate new approaches against meaningful baselines and determine where additional methodological complexity is—or is not—justified.
Build maintainable research software with clear documentation, testing, version control, and reproducible workflows.
Scale computational methods to large datasets using cloud or high-performance computing environments.
Communicate findings, limitations, and recommendations clearly to scientific and technical collaborators.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Basic Qualifications)

PhD in computer science, machine learning, computational biology, bioinformatics, statistics, bioengineering, physics, or a related quantitative field with 2+ years of experience.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing machine-learning, optimization, probabilistic, or other computational methods for biological or molecular data.
Strong Python programming skills and experience with modern scientific-computing or machine-learning frameworks.
Experience working with biological sequence, structure, or another form of molecular data.
Evidence of rigorous model evaluation, including appropriate baselines, validation strategies, and interpretation of model limitations.
Ability to translate an open-ended scientific question into a tractable computational research plan.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

Experience with RNA or mRNA biology, design, engineering, or therapeutics.
Experience with generative models, transformers, graph neural networks, representation learning, active learning, Bayesian optimization, or multi-objective optimization.
Familiarity with RNA secondary structure, ensemble properties, or chemical-probing data such as SHAPE.
Experience integrating high-throughput experimental or NGS-derived measurements with computational models.
Experience developing reusable scientific software rather than one-off analysis scripts.
Experience with cloud or distributed computing environments.
Publications, patents, or open-source work demonstrating a substantive contribution to algorithm or method development.
Ability to work effectively across computational and experimental teams.

Our Working Model

As we build our company, we have always believed that an in-person culture is critical to our success. This role is 100% onsite, reflecting the importance of being physically present to support the work, collaborate closely with colleagues, and contribute to our site-based operations.

Working onsite enables real-time collaboration, strong team connections, direct mentorship, and the hands-on partnership needed to deliver our mission. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.

Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.

Pay & Benefits

At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work.
That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $145,900.00 - $234,200.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.

About Moderna

Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.

By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.

We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.

If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.

Basic Qualifications

Education Requirements:

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering, or related Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics field, plus a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience; or Master's degree, plus 6 years relevant experience.

Due to the nature of work performed within our facilities, U.S. citizenship is required.

Responsibilities For This Position

ROLE AND POSITION OBJECTIVES:

The AI Software Engineer, Applications and Agents will design, code, test, evaluate, secure, deploy, and improve full-stack AI products. The engineer will work directly with users, domain experts, product owners, and technical teams to move from problem definition to working product and measurable outcome.

The role combines software engineering, enterprise data, and AI to build secure applications and re-engineer operations. The engineer will use approved cloud services, models, APIs, data, identity, security, and scalable application patterns across Azure and AWS. This is a hands-on individual-contributor software-engineering position.

What You Will Do

Build Production AI Applications and Agents

Design, write, test, integrate, review, deploy, and operate production AI applications, agents, APIs, services, and user experiences .
Work directly with business and engineering teams to build production-scale AI applications, agents, integrations, and end-to-end enterprise workflows .
Build agentic workflows using planning, reasoning, context management, retrieval, tool use, human approval, and multi-agent collaboration where appropriate.
Integrate approved commercial, open-weight, self-hosted, and GDMS-controlled models through secure interfaces and runtime services.
Develop full-stack products using modern frontend, backend, API, event-driven, data, and cloud-native engineering patterns.
Own delivery from ambiguous problem definition through architecture, implementation, testing, production release, adoption, support, and lifecycle improvement.
Build secure enterprise integrations with business systems, engineering tools, data services, identity, authorization, and workflow platforms.

Engineer AI Quality, Evaluation, and Safety

Define measurable product-quality, task-success, groundedness, safety, latency, reliability, and consumption criteria with product owners and AI Reliability Engineering.
Build automated evaluation pipelines, representative test suites, golden datasets, regression tests, integration tests, automated raters, and human-review workflows.
Evaluate prompts, instructions, context, retrieval, tools, model configurations, routing, and fallback behavior against approved use cases.
Implement controls for hallucination, prompt injection, data leakage, unsafe tool use, excessive autonomy, cross-tenant access, and policy violations.
Use red teaming, failure testing, observability, production feedback, and incident learning to improve application and agent behavior.

Deliver Secure and Supportable Products

Use approved CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, release, artifact, security, and evidence workflows to move products from source through supported production.
Build authentication, authorization, secrets, audit, data-protection, approval, stop, rollback, and recovery behavior into the product design.
Instrument metrics, logs, traces, quality signals, agent actions, model calls, tool use, latency, consumption, failure behavior, and user outcomes.
Serve as an engineering escalation point for complex application failures; troubleshoot across application, model, retrieval, tool, data, identity, network, and platform layers; and implement permanent corrections. Ongoing application support remains with the designated sustainment organization following transition.
Convert defects, incidents, and user feedback into regression tests, permanent engineering corrections, and reusable platform improvements.

Work Directly with Business and Mission Teams

Partner with functions, programs, engineers, and domain experts to decompose work, identify appropriate AI and non-AI solutions, and define measurable outcomes.
Re-engineer operational processes to reduce manual effort, improve flow and controls, and create scalable workflows that combine people, automation, and AI.
Develop prototypes only when needed to resolve uncertainty, then either productionize, transfer, or stop the work based on evidence.
Translate repeated product and workflow needs into reusable components, reference applications, templates, and integrations.
Measure adoption, task success, quality, cycle time, productivity, reliability, and mission or business impact after release.

Provide Senior Advanced Technical Direction

Work with limited instruction on complex, ambiguous, and undefined challenges that require original engineering judgment.
Define the scope, architecture, engineering evidence, schedule, risks, and acceptance expectations for work personally executed or technically led.
Provide code and architecture review, pairing, mentoring, and technical work direction without requiring people-management authority.
Use AI coding agents and engineering assistants for implementation, testing, review, diagnosis, documentation, and delivery while maintaining verification and accountability.
Keep current with commercial generative AI, agent, software-engineering, evaluation, cloud, security, and product-delivery practices; introduce validated improvements into GDMS engineering.

Required

Bachelor's degree in Software Engineering or a related Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics field plus a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience; or a master's degree plus a minimum of 6 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrated advanced or expert proficiency coding, testing, integrating, documenting, deploying, and operating production software products.
Strong production coding ability in Python and at least one additional language such as TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++, C#, or Rust.
Experience delivering full-stack or backend cloud applications using APIs, data stores, eventing, authentication, authorization, testing, CI/CD, telemetry, and production support.
Hands-on experience building generative AI applications, agents, RAG solutions, tool-using workflows, or comparable intelligent systems in production.

Translate business problems into scalable technical solutions using modern AI engineering best practices

added.title: Generative AI Engineer
added.description:
Position Summary

Magpie Health Analytics is seeking an experienced AI Engineer to design, build, and operate secure, trustworthy generative AI solutions that help our healthcare clients deliver faster, more consistent access to authoritative program guidance.

Key Responsibilities

Our clients are government health payers. Your primary responsibility is to design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain an AI-enabled decision-support capability that allows users to search and navigate large bodies of program documentation (statutes, regulations, rules, and guidance) using natural language. The solution will first support internal customers and will later be extended to external, public-facing users. You will work in collaboration with project managers, data engineers, full stack developers, analysts, and client stakeholders to ensure the successful implementation of the client solution. The AI Engineer duties include:

Design, develop, and maintain generative AI solutions that ground large language model (LLM) responses in authoritative source documentation.
Build and maintain document ingestion pipelines, including parsing, chunking, metadata tagging, embedding generation, and vector/semantic search indexing.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams and subject matter experts to understand user needs and translate them into requirements, prompts, and evaluation criteria.
Implement responses with source citations and direct links to the underlying documentation to ensure traceability.
Design and implement guardrails, including content filtering, scope restrictions, PII/PHI protections, and refusal handling for out-of-scope questions.
Develop evaluation frameworks and test sets to measure retrieval quality, answer accuracy, groundedness, and consistency; monitor and tune performance over time.
Deploy and operate solutions within approved AWS services and federal security controls, supporting documentation needed for security authorization and AI governance reviews.
Implement logging, monitoring, and audit trails to support transparency, cost management, and responsible AI oversight.
Write clean, reusable, and well-documented code, and participate in code reviews, testing, and deployment processes.
Stay up to date with emerging AI technologies, models, and federal AI guidance.

Educational Requirements

A master's degree in computer science, data science, engineering, or another relevant field.

Qualifications

5+ years of experience developing software and cloud-based solutions, with demonstrated recent experience designing and deploying LLM or generative AI applications.
Strong proficiency in Python and experience with modern LLM APIs, SDKs, orchestration frameworks, and AI/ML libraries (e.g., Hugging Face, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or equivalent).
Hands-on experience designing and deploying generative AI solutions, including embeddings, vector databases, and hybrid/semantic search.
Experience with AWS AI and data services such as Amazon Bedrock, Amazon OpenSearch, Amazon Kendra, SageMaker, Lambda, or S3.
Experience with prompt and context engineering, LLM evaluation, and techniques for reducing hallucinations and ensuring answers are grounded in source material.
Designing AI applications to support multiple foundation models/providers and evaluating models based on accuracy, latency, cost, security, and use-case requirements.
Experience with Agile software development methodologies.
Experience with building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines, testing, and deploying infrastructure using services such as GitHub Actions, CloudFormation, Terraform, and/or Jenkins.
Excellent problem-solving and communication skills, including the ability to explain AI capabilities and limitations to non-technical stakeholders.

This scientist will play a leading role in advancing approaches for cancer vaccine design, identifying high-impact opportunities for algorithmic innovation, and developing new machine-learning approaches to improve antigen selection.

This is an opportunity to define the next generation of computational methods used to select antigens for personalized cancer vaccines. The successful candidate will combine deep expertise in machine learning and computational biology with strong scientific judgment and a hands-on approach to model development. They will define modeling strategies, data requirements, and validation frameworks, as well as develop novel computational methodologies. Demonstrated ability to independently define scientific problems, develop novel computational approaches, and critically evaluate model performance, robustness, and generalization.
Experience integrating and learning from heterogeneous, noisy, incomplete, or high-dimensional biological datasets.

Overview:

The Analytics and AI methods at Scale (AAIMS) group in the National Center for Computational Science (NCCS) is hiring Senior Research Scientist to push the frontier of AI for science such as: scientific reasoning, federated & collaborative learning, and reinforcement learning (RL) for self-improving models on leadership-class supercomputers. You’ll help design, train, and evaluate AI systems that plan, reason, and take actions to accelerate discovery across domains (materials, chemistry, climate, fusion, biology, and more).

NCCS operates the Frontier exascale supercomputer and world-class data facilities. This role sits at the intersection of AI at scale and HPC, giving you unmatched resources to prototype new ideas, run large ablations, and translate methods into scientific impact.

Examples of Focus Areas:

Agentic AI for Science: Autonomous and tool-using agents for experiment design, simulation steering, data collection, and lab/compute orchestration; planning and memory; multi-agent collaboration.
Scientific Reasoning: Program/path-of-thought, tool-augmented and retrieval-augmented reasoning; uncertainty quantification and calibrated decisions.
RL & Self-Improving Models: RLHF/RLAIF, online RL, self-play, open-ended discovery, reward modeling, curriculum/active learning, data selection, iterative post-training, safety alignment and guardrails.
Foundation Models for Science @ Scale: Pretraining, instruction tuning, continued pretraining, Mixture-of-Experts; distributed training/inference (FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM, tensor/sequence parallelism); scalable evaluation pipelines for reasoning and agents.
Federated & Collaborative Learning: Cross-silo training across institutions and facilities; privacy-preserving learning (secure aggregation, differential privacy, MPC/HE); personalization under heterogeneity; governance-aware data/model sharing; collaborative evaluation.

The NCCS is the home of the world’s first exascale supercomputer Frontier. Our Leadership Computing Program (OLCF) provides world class computing facilities to applications across all computational domains and disciplines. We are an inclusive dynamic environment that welcomes those with initiative and creativity.

Major Duties/Responsibilities:

Develop and coordinate division activities in HPC-AI with cross-cutting initiatives in the laboratory by establishing forward-looking centers of excellence.
Lead and collaborate with internal and external researchers on a variety of extreme-scale AI/ML research and projects.
Lead in authoring peer reviewed papers, technical papers, reports, and proposals. Advance personal and staff contributions in leading professional, academic, and research organizations.
Advance personal and staff contributions in leading professional, academic, and research organizations.
Team Building & Mentorship: Provide mentorship to postdocs, students, and junior staff, fostering long-term career development.
Stakeholder Engagement: Effectively communicate vision, strategy, and progress to DOE sponsors, industrial partners, and international collaborators.

Basic Qualifications:

PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a field closely related to the job duties of this position.
A minimum of 6 years of relevant research experience outside of Ph.D.
Demonstrated research in cross-cutting fields of HPC and/or AI.

Preferred Qualifications:

Demonstrated leadership in conceiving, planning, and delivering large-scale HPC-AI projects with measurable scientific or technological impact.
Experience securing competitive funding (e.g., DOE, NSF, DARPA, industry consortia) and leading multi-institution proposals.
Recognition by the broader community – invited talks, keynote addresses, professional society awards, or major benchmarks.
Impactful open-source contributions to HPC or AI framework (e.g., Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, Ray, Distributed RL)
Interdisciplinary collaboration experience – working with domain scientist (climate, material, fusion, biology) to translate methods into real discoveries.
Strategic vision – ability to identify long-term research directions at the intersection of AI, HPC and domain sciences.

Special Requirements:

For employment at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), a Real ID compliant form of identification will be required. Additionally, ORNL is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which requires a favorable post-employment background investigation.
To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a Federal Tier 1 background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.
For foreign national candidates: If you have not resided in the U.S. for three consecutive years, you are not eligible for the PIV credential and instead will need to obtain a favorable Local Site Specific Only (LSSO) risk determination to maintain employment. Once you meet the three-year residency requirement, you will be required to obtain a PIV credential to maintain employment.

added.description:
Discover your potential. Build your legacy.

Go the distance with Capital Group

At Capital Group, we go the distance — for our people, our clients, and each other. As a global, privately held firm with more than 95 years of history, we believe meaningful careers, like meaningful investing, are built over the long term. That’s why we invest in our associates with the same conviction we bring to our clients — through career growth, purpose-driven work, whole-person wellness, and rewards that recognize your contributions. Here, you’ll find the opportunity, global scale and support to unlock your potential and build a career that lasts.

The role

As an AI Engineer Lead, you’ll partner with investment professionals and business partners to turn ambiguous problems into production AI solutions that improve investment processes and business outcomes. You’ll lead discovery, shape the technical approach, write the code, and own solutions through deployment and operation. This hands-on role connects the people who understand the problem with the AI platform that powers the answer, while helping set a responsible engineering standard for generative AI across the firm.

As an AI Engineer Lead, you’ll partner with investment professionals and business partners to turn ambiguous problems into production AI solutions that improve investment processes and business outcomes. You’ll lead discovery, shape the technical approach, write the code, and own solutions through deployment and operation. This hands-on role connects the people who understand the problem with the AI platform that powers the answer, while helping set a responsible engineering standard for generative AI across the firm.

The team

You’ll work across investment, business, platform, product, engineering, risk, compliance, information security, and data-governance partners. Together, you’ll build and operate generative AI capabilities that connect enterprise data and systems with practical workflows for investment professionals and business teams. You’ll also turn successful approaches into reusable tools, patterns, and playbooks that help the broader organization deliver AI solutions safely and consistently.

Your impact

Partner with investment professionals and business teams to understand workflows, identify high-value opportunities, and turn ambiguous needs into clear technical specifications.
Design, build, and operate production generative AI applications, including copilots, assistants, knowledge-search experiences, and agentic workflows.
Architect end-to-end retrieval-augmented generation pipelines across parsing, ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector storage, retrieval, and prompt management.
Build agents that complete multi-step work within explicit, auditable boundaries, with guardrails that keep behavior safe and predictable.
Define acceptance criteria and evaluation harnesses that measure correctness, latency, hallucination, and regression risk before and after release.
Own solutions from discovery through production, adding observability, cost tracking, audit trails, documentation, runbooks, and architectural diagrams so others can operate and extend them.
Integrate AI solutions with enterprise data, APIs, and MLOps or LLMOps tooling while applying sound system-design, distributed-systems, FinOps, and cost-optimization practices.
Embed responsible AI, security, privacy, compliance, identity and access management, encryption, human oversight, and audit logging into each solution, then codify proven approaches for reuse.

What you’ll bring

A minimum of 10 years of professional software engineering experience, with strong proficiency in Python or a comparable modern programming language.
Hands-on production experience building and shipping large language model applications, including prompt design, retrieval, agent development, evaluation, and guardrails.
Demonstrated experience designing end-to-end retrieval-augmented generation pipelines and integrating AI solutions with production systems.
Strong knowledge of system design, APIs, distributed systems, cloud-native development, and the architectural foundations required to own reliable production services.
A disciplined approach to evaluating and testing non-deterministic systems, with evaluation criteria and safeguards built into the engineering lifecycle.
Strong communication and discovery skills, including the ability to lead working sessions, write clearly, and explain technical concepts to mixed audiences with a collaborative approach.
High agency and sound judgment in ambiguous, regulated environments, including the ability to balance scope, speed, quality, and operational risk.
A bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience, plus experience implementing production security, privacy, and compliance controls such as IAM, encryption, audit logging, and data governance.

What You’ll Get

When you go the distance for our clients, we go the distance for you. You’ll grow through mentoring, leadership programs and tuition reimbursement, and do work that matters at a firm managing $3T+ in AUM for millions of investors worldwide. We invest in your whole life too – with comprehensive wellness and mental health support, family-first benefits, competitive pay with performance and profitability bonuses and a company-funded retirement plan. And as a privately held firm built for the long term, we offer the opportunity and support to build a career that lasts.
